notes: **Work:** $W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d}$. Dot product gives a scalar measuring energy transfer. Zero work when force is perpendicular to displacement.
**Torque:** $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$. Cross product gives a vector representing rotational effect. Magnitude is $rF\sin\theta$.
**Angular momentum:** $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} = \vec{r} \times m\vec{v}$. For a particle in circular motion, $L = mvr$ (when $\vec{r} \perp \vec{v}$).
**Conservation of angular momentum:** when net external torque is zero, $\vec{L}$ is constant. A skater pulling in arms reduces $r$, so $\omega$ increases to keep $L$ constant.

**Why cross product fits rotation:** torque and angular momentum are inherently rotational quantities. The cross product automatically produces a vector perpendicular to the plane of rotation, matching the axis direction given by the right-hand rule.
